Subject: PO vs Card — procurement & payment path for Redwood pilot

Hi Sarah — great to meet you on the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps on the procurement/payment path so we can get your pilot scheduled: 

1) Procurement readiness: you mentioned BigCorp typically uses a PO for vendor spend > $25k but will accept card for smaller purchases. For an initial 3-month pilot (expected cost in the $8-12k range) you said you need to confirm whether AP will allow a credit card or if we should route through a PO.

2) Vendor onboarding: AP will need our vendor packet and W-9; I attached a one-page PO template and our vendor onboarding form to speed up things. If AP requires vendor setup in Coupa (or Ariba) we can provide the necessary fields and a sample invoice format.

3) Commercial path/options: options we discussed — (A) pilot on card to accelerate start, then move to PO if you decide to scale; (B) submit a PO now and we kickoff as soon as AP issues the PO number. If there are marketplace procurement flows you want to use (marketplace purchase with pre-approved contract), let me know — we can work with marketplace team.

Next steps: 
- Sarah: confirm whether AP will allow card for this pilot or if a PO is required. If PO required, please share the expected PO number timeline and any vendor setup forms.
- Marissa: I’m looping you in to help with contract templating & pricing for a pilot SOW (we talked about a reduced commitment option).
- Aditya: can you confirm whether we have any finance constraints for accepting card vs PO for this customer and if there are any upfront invoice/credit terms to note?

Thanks — want to keep momentum and lock a start date for next week if possible.

Best,
Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Lauren / team — quick finance note from our side: 

- We can accept corporate card for pilot transactions under $25k; card transactions are processed via Stripe and are immediate. There are no special onboarding requirements for card payments beyond the standard billing contact and invoice email.
- If BigCorp prefers PO, we require a PO # on the invoice and standard net-30 terms by default. For customers requesting net-60 or special credit terms we need the credit approval process which takes longer (2-3 weeks).
- One red flag: some enterprise AP teams insist on vendor portal onboarding which delays start until vendor setup is complete. If BigCorp wants to avoid that ramp friction, card is faster.

Marissa — if we move forward on PO path, please prep the short pilot SOW and an invoice template that includes the PO # field. Lauren — attaching the two files you already included here for record.

Thanks,
Aditya
